catalog_citation: Reh, Mechthild (1985). Die Krongo-Sprache (Nìinò Mó-Dì): Beschreibung, Texte, Wörterverzeichnis. Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 12. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. — as summarised in StressTyp2 passage 1224 (lect 628 Krongo).
catalog_quote: Stress is not thoroughly researched. It is located on the first high toned syllable. In words with only low tones it is located on the first syllable (Reh 1985, 78).In words with affixes the location of stress is determined by:1. Tones in the affixes2. Tones in the root3. Number of syllables in the root4. Vowel length in the first syllable of the root If the root is monosyllabic, or contains only low tones and a short vowel in the first syllable or has the sequence LH.There are some lexical oppositions.If the word is sufficiently long, high toned prefixes may get a secondary stress.

sources.citation: Hall, Ed and Marian Hall. 2004. Kadugli-Krongo. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 57-68. SIL-Sudan.
sources.quote: 'The tone system has not been fully analysed for any of the Kadugli-Krongo languages. Reh (1983) establishes High and Low tone for Krongo-Tabanya and states that it is significant both lexically and grammatically.' ... 'The other Kadugli-Krongo languages that we have studied also have two tones, with a considerable amount of pitch conditioning.' No statement about word stress/accent in Krongo anywhere in the article (the 'Stress' passages later in the volume belong to Duerksen's Dinka-Nuer article, pp.69ff).
